title: [Bug]: Identity entry in packed_modules_mapping silently disables layer_quant_config (Quark)
body:
### The bug

An identity entry in `packed_modules_mapping` — a mapping of a module to itself, e.g.
`"gate_up_proj": ["gate_up_proj"]` — silently disables `layer_quant_config` for that module. The
layer falls back to `global_quant_config` instead, so a mixed-precision checkpoint gets built with
the wrong scheme and fails at weight load with a shape mismatch.

In `vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/quark/quark.py`, both lookup paths treat
`shard_name == layer_name` as "no shard information available":

```python
# get_layer_quant_config_from_name
shard_name = layer_name.replace(proj_name, shard_proj_name)
if shard_name != layer_name:
    config = self.get_layer_quant_config_from_name(shard_name)
else:
    config = None                      # <-- identity entry -> no config

# _find_matched_config
if shard_name == layer_name:
    config = fallback_config           # <-- identity entry -> global scheme
```

For a genuine fusion (`fused_qkv_a_proj` -> `[q_a_proj, kv_a_proj_with_mqa]`) that is right: the
shard names differ, and the entries are looked up individually. For an identity entry the
substitution is a no-op, and the code concludes there is nothing to look up — even though
`layer_quant_config` may contain the layer under its own name.

### Who this affects

Identity entries are an established pattern in-tree, not a mistake by checkpoint authors:

```
vllm/model_executor/models/plamo3.py:375     "gate_up_proj": ["gate_up_proj"],
vllm/model_executor/models/glm4_1v.py:1769   "gate_up_proj": ["gate_up_proj"],
vllm/model_executor/models/molmo.py:1313     "gate_up_proj": ["gate_up_proj"],  # language model
```

Any Quark checkpoint that uses `layer_quant_config` to give one of these modules a different
scheme than the global one is affected. It is silent until load: no warning, no log line, just the
global scheme applied where a per-layer scheme was specified.

### Reproduction

GLM-5.3-Flash, Quark MXFP4 checkpoint with `layer_quant_config` marking the dense MLPs as
block-FP8 while the MoE experts are MXFP4:

```
AssertionError: language_model.model.layers.0.mlp.gate_up_proj shard=0
  param=(24576, 2048)/torch.uint8      <- built as MXFP4 from global_quant_config
  loaded=(12288, 4096)/torch.float8_e4m3fn   <- checkpoint has FP8
```

The sibling `down_proj` (not in `packed_modules_mapping`) resolves correctly to
`QuarkW8A8Fp8PerBlock` in the same model; only `gate_up_proj` takes the fallback. Traced with a
print in `get_scheme`:

```
[TRACE] ...layers.0.mlp.gate_up_proj -> QuarkOCP_MX     dtype=fp4    packed=True
[TRACE] ...layers.0.mlp.down_proj    -> QuarkW8A8Fp8PerBlock dtype=fp8_e4m3 packed=False
```

and the mapping itself:

```
[TRACE-MAP] gate_up_proj -> ['gate_up_proj']
[TRACE-MAP]   shard gate_up_proj: name=...layers.0.mlp.gate_up_proj  same=True  hit=False
```

`hit=False` although the key is present in `layer_quant_config`.

### Fix

Look the layer up directly when the shard name is the layer name. Extracting the direct lookup out
of `get_layer_quant_config_from_name` into a small helper and calling it from both places is
enough:

```python
def _direct_layer_quant_config(self, layer_name: str) -> dict[str, Any] | None:
    layer_quant_config = cast(dict[str, Any],
                              self.quant_config.get("layer_quant_config") or {})
    for name_pattern, config in layer_quant_config.items():
        matches = (layer_name in name_pattern if "*" not in name_pattern
                   else fnmatch.fnmatch(layer_name, name_pattern))
        if matches:
            return config
    return None
```

then in `get_layer_quant_config_from_name` use it for the `shard_name == layer_name` branch, and in
`_find_matched_config` try it before falling back to `fallback_config`. Behaviour for genuine
fusions and for models without identity entries is unchanged.

I am happy to open a PR with this plus a regression test if the approach looks right. Verified
locally on ROCm (gfx950, ROCm 7.2.3) with GLM-5.3-Flash; after the change `gate_up_proj` resolves
to `QuarkW8A8Fp8PerBlock` and the shape mismatch is gone.
